claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I do. I have one child, Alex, who's 7 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have Alex, who is 7 years old.

**Do you live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's the thing - I actually don't live in the UK at the moment. But Alex does live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

**Which country do you currently live in with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm currently living in Spain with Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you letting me know that. This is an important detail for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have any other connection to the UK (such as being a Crown servant)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful.

**Do you have any income, or are you working at all currently?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I do have some income, yes. Why do you ask?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I ask because there are specific rules about Child Benefit eligibility when you live abroad. The rules depend on your circumstances, including your employment status and income.

**Are you currently employed or self-employed, or do you have income from another source?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm employed, yes. I work here in Spain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Are you working for a UK employer, or are you working for a Spanish employer (or another non-UK employer)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I work for a Spanish employer.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

**Is your work in Spain considered to be "normal work" in the Spanish social security system - meaning you're paying social security contributions there?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. I pay into the Spanish social security system.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful for understanding your situation.

**Are you paying National Insurance contributions to the UK, or have you been paying UK National Insurance contributions recently?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not paying National Insurance to the UK anymore since I've been living and working in Spain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have a good understanding of your situation now, but I need to ask one more important question:

**How long have you been living in Spain with Alex? In other words, when did you move there?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I've been living here for about a year and a half now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided, I need to explain the situation regarding your eligibility:

You are living abroad (in Spain) with your child Alex. According to UK Child Benefit rules, you may be able to get Child Benefit if you live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant. However, the specific eligibility for living abroad depends on factors such as:

- Whether you're working in a country with a social security agreement with the UK
- Whether you're paying contributions that count towards UK benefits
- Your right to reside status

Since you're working for a Spanish employer and paying into the Spanish social security system (rather than UK National Insurance), your eligibility becomes more complex and would depend on whether Spain has a relevant social security agreement with the UK and how that affects your benefit rights.

**To give you a definitive answer, I need to know: Do you have any connection to the UK that might affect your eligibility - for example, are you still registered with a UK address, do you own property in the UK, or do you receive any UK benefits or pensions?**

This will help me determine whether you would qualify under the rules for living abroad.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't have any of those connections. I've fully moved to Spain - no UK address registration, no property there, and I'm not receiving any UK benefits or pensions.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. I now have sufficient details to make a determination about your Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

Unfortunately, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex at this time**.

**Why?** While you do live with Alex (which is normally a key requirement), you are currently living outside the UK in Spain. Child Benefit rules allow you to claim if you live abroad in certain circumstances, such as if you're a Crown servant or have specific rights under social security agreements. Since you're working for a Spanish employer, paying into the Spanish social security system, and have no remaining connections to the UK, you don't meet these qualifying criteria.

**What you could do:**
- If you were to return to live in the UK with Alex, you would become eligible for Child Benefit
- You may want to contact HMRC directly for specific advice about your situation, as there may be nuances related to social security agreements that I'm not able to fully assess

I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office at HMRC if you'd like to discuss your specific circumstances in more detail.
